gbm_population_evidence.quote: Tislelizumab (One Anti-PD-1 Antibody) Plus Low-dose Bevacizumab for Bevacizumab Refractory Recurrent Glioblastoma

candidate_evidence.quote: The purpose of this study is to evaluate the clinical efficacy and safety of Tislelizumab (one anti-PD-1 antibody same as nivolumab approved in China) in combination with bevacizumab

treatment_setting_evidence.quote: in patients with recurrent or progressive glioblastoma (GBM) who have progressed on bevacizumab with or without PTEN or TERT gene mutations.

role_evidence.quote: Tislelizumab (one anti-PD-1 antibody same as nivolumab approved in China)

agents.drug_class_hint: anti-VEGF monoclonal antibody (established GBM therapy), given at low dose

source_quote.quote: Patients with bevacizumab-refractory recurrent glioma with PTEN or TERT gene mutations,determined according to the dynamics of TISF (Tumor in Situ Fluid) ctDNA.

coder_notes: Bevacizumab: an established GBM therapy given at 'low-dose' (3 mg/kg) named in the title in a bevacizumab-refractory population; coded established_therapy_experiment (could alternatively be soc_backbone since patients already progressed on bevacizumab); either way not a candidate and tislelizumab is the only investigational agent. Exclusion criterion 7 ('Previous bevacizumab') contradicts the bevacizumab-refractory population. PTEN/TERT mutation status (TISF ctDNA) assigns patients to Cohort 1 (mutated) vs Cohort 2 (not mutated); no mechanistic link to tislelizumab stated, so not candidate-matched. Outcome text mentions durvalumab in passing (likely template error); not listed. Inclusion only says 'glioma' but title and conditions name glioblastoma.
